fullAnalysis: Puzzle #677 gives you five clues — Sun, Wrap, Cocktail, Wedding, and Little black — that look like a mix of weather, cooking, events, and colours. The surface meanings could easily point toward party themes or seasonal occasions, which is a deliberate misdirect. The actual connector is the word 'dress': every clue forms a specific, named dress style.

Sundress, wrap dress, cocktail dress, wedding dress, and little black dress are all established fashion terms that appear regularly in magazines, retail, and everyday conversation. None of them require obscure fashion knowledge — these are mainstream phrases that most people encounter routinely.
solutionNarrative: I tried the event angle first. Cocktail and Wedding both felt like occasions, which sent me toward party themes and formal events. But Sun and Wrap didn't belong in that framing at all. I stepped back and changed the question from 'what occasions?' to 'what type of dress?' — and the whole board resolved instantly.

Sundress, wrap dress, cocktail dress, wedding dress, little black dress. Every clue confirmed the pattern cleanly, including Little black, which I initially read as two separate words rather than one compound modifier. Once I treated it as a single unit, the connection was obvious. Five for five with no exceptions.

wordHints.Sun: Sundress is a standard warm-weather clothing term and often the quickest anchor on this board.
wordHints.Wrap: Wrap dress is a well-known fashion silhouette that confirms the dress category.
wordHints.Cocktail: Cocktail dress is a classic formal-wear phrase — despite sounding like an event clue, it names a specific dress style.
wordHints.Wedding: Wedding dress is one of the most fixed fashion phrases in everyday language.
wordHints.Little black: Little black dress is the iconic fashion phrase, making it the final clean confirmation of the category.

lessons.title: Event clues can name objects, not occasions
lessons.body: Cocktail and Wedding both sound like events, but they complete dress phrases rather than pointing to occasion themes. If multiple clues feel like occasions or settings, test whether they all name the same type of object instead.

lessons.title: Switching the frame unlocks the board
lessons.body: The clues only make sense as a group once you ask 'what type of dress?' instead of 'what occasion?'. When one framing produces mixed results across the clues, change the question you are asking — the right connector becomes obvious immediately.

lessons.title: Multi-word clues are tested as a single unit
lessons.body: Little black is two words, but little black dress is a single, fixed cultural phrase. Pinpoint uses multi-word fragments occasionally; treat them as one compound modifier and apply the connector to the whole phrase, not just the last word.
